content_metadata.description: An educational video detailing the mechanism of G protein receptors, how they are activated and deactivated, presented through animation with narration.

qAndA.question: What molecule binds to the receptor site on the outside of the cell?
What is attached to the alpha subunit of the G protein in its inactive state?
What replaces GDP on the alpha subunit when the G protein is activated?

qAndA.answer: It eventually becomes inactive by removing a phosphate from GTP, converting it back to GDP.
qAndA.question: What happens to the alpha subunit after it separates from the beta and gamma subunits?

qAndA.answer: They recombine and return to their original inactive state, ready for another activation cycle.
qAndA.question: What happens to the G protein subunits after the ligand unbinds from the receptor?

activities.description: Ligand binding: A ligand (yellow triangle) approaches and binds to the receptor site.
G protein activation: The G protein changes conformation, and GTP replaces GDP on the alpha subunit.
Alpha subunit separation: The activated alpha subunit separates from the beta and gamma subunits.
Ligand unbinding: The ligand detaches from the receptor site.
G protein inactivation: The alpha subunit removes a phosphate from GTP, leaving GDP bound.
G protein recombination: The G protein subunits recombine.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Visuals assist in explaining the molecular processes detailed by the narration.

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator introduces the receptor site and ligand.
The G protein and its bound GDP are introduced.
The ligand binds to the receptor site, initiating the activation process.
The G protein undergoes conformational change, and GTP replaces GDP.
The activated alpha subunit separates from the other subunits.
The ligand detaches from the receptor.
The alpha subunit dephosphorylates GTP to GDP, becoming inactive.
The G protein subunits recombine to their initial state.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: As a receptor site for a small molecule called a ligand, exposed on the outside of the cell,
the portion of the receptor on the inside of the cell can bind to the G protein, which
has a guana-scene diphosphate attached to its alpha subunit. When the ligand binds to the receptor
site on the outside of the cell membrane, the G protein changes confirmation, and guana-scene
triphosphate replaces the guana-scene diphosphate on the alpha subunit of the G protein.
The activated alpha subunit then separates from the beta and gamma subunits. This step
can be repeated as long as the ligand remains bound to the receptor. When the ligand separates
from the receptor site, additional G proteins are no longer activated. Inactivation of the alpha subunit
occurs when its own phosphorylase activity removes a phosphate from the guana-scene triphosphate,
leaving guana-scene diphosphate bound to the subunit. The G protein subunits then
recombine and attach to the receptor in the cell membrane.
